messages.subject: Regex question
parts:
(I feel slightly lazy posting here instead of figuring out the
solution by myself, but this way at least others who might have
similar issues can also benefit. It's not really a serious problem,
but rather a kind of behavior that I would like to adjust by modifying
my regex.)

I have a text element (tweets) that contains xml-encoded Twitter
messages. I want to strip all XML except for the message body
(enclosed by the <body>-tag). The files look like the snippet below

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!-- some comments -->
<thread><id>User123</id><posts><post><user><username>User123</
username></user><to>@User456</to><date>1229737188</
date><body>blablabla</body></post><post><user><username>User123</
username></user><to></to><body>lalala</body></post></posts>
</thread>

My regex looks like this:
tweets <- gsub(".*?<body>(.*?)</body>.*?", "\\1\n", buffer, perl=T)

It works fine, except for the final information after the last closing
body tag also being matched, returning "...lalala</post></posts></
thread>" instead of just the message text.

I do understand how greedy vs lazy matching and lookahead/lookbehind
work (I think), but I can't figure how to leave out the stuff that
comes after </body>.

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Regex question
parts: > (I feel slightly lazy posting here instead of figuring out the solution by myself, but this way at least others who might have similar issues can also benefit.

That's the spirit!

One problem is that you use lazy matching at the end, where you say
"</body>.*?": the question marks says, go only as far as you need to.
Thus, it stops after zero (the asterisk!), leaving everything in.
However, since you may have several bodies in the tweet, this is what
I can come up with fastest:

x<-"<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?><!-- some comments -->
<thread><id>User123</id><posts><post><user><username>User123</username></user><to>@User456</to><date>1229737188</date><body>blablabla</body></post><post><user><username>User123</username></user><to></to><body>lalala</body></post></posts></thread>"

y1<-unlist(strsplit(x, "<body>"))
y2<-grep("</body>", y1, value=T)
y3<-gsub("</body>.*", "", y2, perl=T)
y3 # tadaa

HTH,

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Regex question
parts:
Oh, and of course this is much (!) better:

exact.matches("(?<=<body>).*?(?=</body>)", x, T, F)[[1]]

messages.author: 1e2f7f65d86e3c66
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: Regex question
parts:
> My regex looks like this:
> tweets <- gsub(".*?<body>(.*?)</body>.*?", "\\1\n", buffer, perl=T)

> It works fine, except for the final information after the last closing
> body tag also being matched, returning "...lalala</post></posts></
> thread>" instead of just the message text.

For a quick and dirty fix you could also just explicitly include the
elements you want removed in the match. If I understand the xml
structure correctly, there will be no opening tags after the final
</body>, so they're all closing tags:

tweets <- gsub(".*?<body>(.*?)</body>.*?(</[^>]+>)*", "\\1\n", buffer, perl=T)
